The point $P(\frac{2}{3},\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ?$ Do not round your answer.

$\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229367/assets/fdddfbe8431756e0e0341ad6576383764eb88519cc0454280ce4d443559d3536.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{2}{3}$ and $y=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{2}{3},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})}{(\frac{2}{3})}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}
$$
